features.title: Rebase weather (M).

details.title: Rebase weather (M).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Rebase weather (M).** In the interactive-rebase list, each row gets a sun, a cloud or a storm for whether it applies cleanly at that position. The icons update while you move a commit, so you see the storm before you drop it. Hovering a storm names the conflicting files and says whether Mergiraf solves them. The todo list is replayed in memory, debounced, with results cached by (parent tree, commit).
  _Closest:_ [I-Rebase](https://github.com/13hakta/i-rebase), a VS Code extension with a manual "check conflicts" button based on file overlap.
implementation_scope: Replay the current interactive-rebase todo after reorder/action changes, debounced and cached by parent-tree and commit.
Draw per-row clean/uncertain/conflict weather; show conflict paths and Mergiraf likelihood on hover.
Handle dropped/squashed/fixup/reword steps correctly, old Git capabilities, cancellation and stale results; no working-tree mutation.

features.title: Lost and found by content (S–M).

details.title: Lost and found by content (S–M).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Lost and found by content (S–M).** "I had a function `parse_header` on Tuesday and it's gone": type what you remember. gitcraft searches the reflogs, dropped stashes, dangling commits and dangling blobs (things once staged but never committed), and shows the hits on a timeline. Each one can come back as a branch, a file or a stash. It uses `git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs`, then `cat-file --batch` and a grep.
  _Closest:_ Git Extensions' _Recover lost objects_, which covers commits only.
implementation_scope: User-initiated text search over reflog-reachable and unreachable commits, dropped stashes, and dangling blobs from staged-but-uncommitted data.
Use fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs and bounded cat-file batching/content search in background; show timeline and provenance.
Recover matches as a new branch, file or stash; cancellation, binary/large-object limits and non-destructive restoration previews.

Full src search has no lost-and-found/content-recovery feature.

features.title: Drafts of the working tree (L, opt-in).

details.title: Drafts of the working tree (L, opt-in).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Drafts of the working tree (L, opt-in).** Snapshot the working changes at pauses and before checkouts or rebases, without visible WIP commits. _Uncommitted changes_ gains _Earlier versions_, so a hunk overwritten by mistake can come back. The index stays separate, the snapshots are protected from gc, and old ones are cleared after a while.
  _Seen in:_ [jj's working-copy commit](https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/working-copy/), JetBrains' Local History.
implementation_scope: Opt-in automatic snapshots at pauses and before checkout/rebase; preserve index separately, tracked and appropriate untracked changes, no visible WIP commits.
Protect snapshots under private refs, expire by retention policy, and show Earlier versions under uncommitted changes.
Inspect/restore files or hunks with guards and an undoable action; survive restarts and keep snapshot overhead bounded.

details.title: Conflicts that can wait (L).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Conflicts that can wait (L).** Run a rebase or restack in its own worktree, and show its conflicts on the graph's nodes. You can go do other work and come back. The original branches don't move until you accept the result.
  _Inspired by:_ [jj's first-class conflicts](https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/conflicts/), [VisualJJ](https://www.visualjj.com/).
implementation_scope: Run rebase/restack in a dedicated persistent worktree; show conflicts on corresponding graph nodes and allow opening/resuming it while ordinary work continues.
Keep original branch refs fixed until explicit accept; publish successful result with ref guards; support discard/continue/abort and restart recovery.

details.title: Changelists (L).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Changelists (L).** Group what you're working on into named lists such as _Feature_, _Cleanup_ and _Debug prints_, each with its own draft message. Commit or set aside (shelve) one list and keep the others. Lists by file could come first; by hunk is harder once the files keep changing.
  _Seen in:_ [JetBrains changelists and shelve](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/commit-and-push-changes.html).
implementation_scope: Named changelists with per-list draft messages, initially file membership, selection-driven commit and shelve/unshelve of one list while preserving others.
Persist membership/drafts; safely handle rename/delete, concurrent edits, conflicts and optional hunk membership when implemented; no cross-list data loss.

Per-branch commit/publish and integration view, stable assignment across edits, conflict handling and recovery when assignments overlap.

details.title: Same code, different machines (L).
details.source_text: - [ ] **Same code, different machines (L).** Link the local, WSL and SSH copies of a project. gitcraft then says something like _the tracked files match; Linux passes, Windows fails_, and expanding that shows why: case collisions, executable bits, line endings, tool versions, chosen git settings. It only ever collects facts from an allowlist, never environment variables or credentials.
implementation_scope: Link local, WSL and SSH copies of a project and compare tracked tree identity plus per-machine test outcomes.
Explain differences via allowlisted facts: case collisions, executable bits, line endings, tool versions and chosen Git config.
Show unknown/stale facts and refuse environment-variable/credential collection; background bounded polling and user refresh.

details.title: Behaviour timeline (L–XL).
details.source_text: - [ ] **Behaviour timeline (L–XL).** Scrub through commits like frames in a video editor and watch something change across them: a command's output, a benchmark number, a rendered screenshot. Click the first frame where it changes to see the commit. Results are cached by tree, command and machine. Results that were never run, or don't repeat the same, are marked as such and never filled in by guessing.
implementation_scope: Command/output, benchmark numeric, or screenshot timeline across a selected commit range with interactive scrubbing to changes.
Run in isolated worktrees and cache by tree, command and machine; retain artifact/output metadata.
Expose never-run, failed, timed-out and non-repeating/flaky states; cancellation, limits and repeat checks, never interpolate unrun results.

details.title: Reviewer echo (M).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Reviewer echo (M).** gitcraft builds a small personal rulebook from the review comments you have written on all forges. Before you push, it checks your outgoing diff against it: _you'd flag this: you asked for no `unwrap()` in handlers_, with a link to your own comment. It runs with your own API key or a local model, and it's opt-in.
  _Closest:_ [cubic](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/ai-that-learns-your-team-s-unwritten-rules), which is hosted, team-wide and works only on pull requests.
implementation_scope: Opt-in personal rulebook imported from viewer-authored review comments across forges, each rule linked to source comment.
Before push, use configured own-key/local model to check outgoing diff and display evidence-backed suggestions.
User can inspect/edit/disable/delete rules; no automatic push blocker or undisclosed external data transfer.
dev_evidence: src/forge reads PR comments for current request; no cross-forge personal rulebook store.

features.title: AI objections that come with a reproducer (L).

details.title: AI objections that come with a reproducer (L).
details.source_text: - [ ] **AI objections that come with a reproducer (L).** Instead of an AI review that says "this might break Unicode", ask it to _Show me_. A model writes a small test, gitcraft runs it against the base and the head, and puts the observed difference next to the hunk. The judgement that the change is wrong stays with the person. Start with one ecosystem, such as Rust unit tests, and run the generated code in a sandbox.
implementation_scope: Ask an optional model to generate a small reproducer/test for a selected review objection, initially Rust.
Execute generated code against base and head inside a real sandbox, with resource/time/network/filesystem limits; capture observed difference next to hunk.
Keep test source, commands, exits and output inspectable; distinguish observed differences from correctness judgements and unknowns.

Existing tests run gitcraft's own suite; no mechanism to run model-generated repository code against paired revisions.

details.title: Review storyboard (M–L).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Review storyboard (M–L).** The author arranges a pull request into a short sequence: the old failure, the invariant, the fix, the result. Each card opens a pinned hunk, a file at a commit, or a test result. When new pushes change what a card points at, the card is marked stale. It's stored with base and head IDs, and the anchors survive rebases through range-diff.
  _Closest:_ [CodeTour](https://github.com/microsoft/codetour), which isn't tied to revisions.
implementation_scope: Author-editable ordered PR story cards for old failure, invariant, fix and result; cards pin hunk, revisioned file or recorded test artifact.
Persist exact base/head anchors, resolve through range-diff after rebase and mark stale/unresolvable cards on new push.
Presentation/navigation UI opens pinned evidence and supports edit/reorder/remove/export/share as appropriate.

details.title: Backport by contract (L).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Backport by contract (L).** Drag a fix onto an older release and give its intended behaviour as a regression test. gitcraft cherry-picks it in a scratch worktree for each target and tells _patch applied_ apart from _test passes_. Any adaptation shows next to the original.
  _Closest:_ [cherry-picker](https://github.com/python/cherry-picker), [Boro](https://github.com/nvidia/boro).
implementation_scope: Choose a fix, target release branches and an explicit regression-test contract; cherry-pick in scratch worktree per target.
Show patch-applied separately from test-passed, adaptations beside original, and unknown/timeout/conflict states.
Guard accepting/publishing results, preserve source branch/worktree and clean up only own scratch state.

details.title: Intent cards (M–L).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Intent cards (M–L).** Before you start, post a short, expiring note such as _changing token lifetime, until 15:00_ on a path or a symbol. Teammates using gitcraft see it next to that code before any commit exists. It travels through a small git ref of its own, never acts as a lock, and shows stale or offline as such.
  _Closest:_ [Heddle's intent leases](https://github.com/zyads/heddle), [GitKraken's overlap warnings](https://help.gitkraken.com/gitkraken-desktop/conflict-prevention/).
implementation_scope: Create short expiring intent notes on a path or symbol before commits; store/synchronize through a dedicated small Git ref.
Other users see relevant notes next to code, expiry/stale/offline state and authorship; no locks or silent editing exclusion.
Explicit sync, bounded retention, conflict-safe multi-author updates and malicious note/path validation.
dev_evidence: No intent/lease ref, metadata schema or contextual note UI in src.
Existing Git notes attach to commits only (and notes UI is itself in open #74).

details.title: Release choreography across repositories (XL).
details.source_text: - [ ] **Release choreography across repositories (XL).** Put the backend, the SDK and the frontend on one board, and state a rule such as _the backend supports both protocols before the SDK switches_. gitcraft rehearses the in-between combinations and works out which release order keeps everything compatible. Planning and tests come first. Publishing comes later and needs its own coordination, since separate servers can't push atomically together.
implementation_scope: Multi-repository release board with versions/branches and explicit compatibility/invariant ordering rules.
Rehearse intermediate cross-repo combinations with configured tests; derive a release order with evidence and surface unsupported/conflicting rules.
Planning/tests precede separately coordinated publishing; persist run/result matrix and partial/unknown states.
dev_evidence: No multi-repo compatibility planner, intermediate-version test matrix or release board in src.
Current app models independent repository tabs.

details.title: Saved views of the graph (M).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Saved views of the graph (M).** Presets such as these:
  - _My unpushed work_
  - _My recent changes and what they depend on_
  - _Descendants of this commit_
  - _Only merges into main_

  Long runs of history in between collapse into a connector you can expand. They pick commits by how they relate to each other, which hiding or soloing branches can't do. They would be built on git revision queries rather than a new query language.
  _Seen in:_ [Sapling ISL](https://sapling-scm.com/docs/addons/isl/), [jj revsets](https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/revsets/), [jjui](https://github.com/idursun/jjui).
implementation_scope: Saved Git revision-query presets: my unpushed work, my recent work+dependencies, descendants of selected commit and only merges into default branch.
Persist saved views, execute queries in background and render selected commits with collapsible connector spans for omitted history.
Expanding connector restores intervening commits; do not confuse branch hide/solo with relation-based filtering.

details.title: Line dossier: why is this line like this? (M–L).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Line dossier: why is this line like this? (M–L).** Right-click a line and pick _Explain history_. A card shows every version of the line, following it through moves and reformatting (`blame -w -C -C -M`, repeated on each commit's parent). Each version shows its commit and the pull request that brought it in. The card also shows **the review comments that were made on those lines in that pull request**, and the linked issue. An optional LLM summary, run on your own key or a local model, cites each card. gitcraft can offer to add formatting-only commits to `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.
  _Closest:_ GitLens line history and its pull-request hovers, which only work on GitHub and don't show review comments.
implementation_scope: Explain history card for a selected line: follow previous versions using blame -w -C -C -M repeatedly through parents, moves/reformatting.
Each version has commit, introducing PR, review comments on corresponding lines and linked issue; show uncertainty/stop boundaries.
Optional local/own-key LLM summary with citations; offer formatting-commit additions to .git-blame-ignore-revs after preview.
dev_evidence: src/repo/file_view/blame.rs:31 loads one ordinary git::blame result; no repeated ancestry trace or PR-line comment join.
No dossier or blame-ignore-revs editor in src.

details.title: Symbol biography (L).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Symbol biography (L).** Pick a function and see its life on a timeline like a video editor's: when it was created, renamed, moved to another file, split and deleted. Scrubbing the timeline steps its body through each version, with the author and pull request of each step. A symbol is found by name with tree-sitter, and by how similar its body is across files linked by rename detection.
  _Closest:_ `git log -L :func:file`, which loses the function once it moves to another file.
implementation_scope: Tree-sitter symbol selection/search and history timeline tracking creation, rename, file moves, split and deletion.
Use rename detection plus body similarity to link versions across files; expose ambiguous matches as such.
Scrub symbol body versions with author/commit/PR and revision-aware navigation.

details.title: What usually comes with this? (M).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **What usually comes with this? (M).** While you stage a change to the serializer, gitcraft notices: _changes like this usually also touch the compatibility fixtures, and those haven't changed_. A click shows the past commits behind the hint. It counts which files change together, leaving out bulk and generated commits. Every hint can be dismissed and shows its evidence.
  _Closest:_ [CodeScene's change coupling](https://codescene.io/docs/guides/technical/change-coupling.html), a hosted analysis that doesn't help while you stage.
implementation_scope: Build evidence of file co-change from historical commits, excluding generated/bulk changes and bounded by age/count.
While staging, suggest usually-coupled missing files and list exact supporting commits; threshold/sample counts visible.
Dismiss per hint/pair, background indexing/cache invalidation; never imply a deterministic requirement from correlation.
dev_evidence: src/repo/detail/changes.rs renders current status only; no historical coupling/hint model.
No co-change/coupling analysis or cache in src.

features.title: Clone options: shallow, partial and sparse (S–M).

details.title: Scrub history with filter-repo (L).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **Scrub history with filter-repo (L).** A separate cleanup flow: pick paths or replacements, rewrite a fresh clone with `git filter-repo`, report the refs it changed, and check the result. Publishing it is its own step, with a reminder that a leaked secret also has to be revoked.
  _Benchmark:_ [git-filter-repo](https://github.com/newren/git-filter-repo/blob/main/Documentation/git-filter-repo.txt).
implementation_scope: Dedicated history cleanup flow selecting paths/replacements, always rewrite a fresh clone with installed git-filter-repo.
Preview planned cleanup, show changed refs and validate resulting objects/history/content; retain recoverable source.
Publishing explicit separate step with reference guards and leaked-secret revocation reminder; never automatically force push.
dev_evidence: No filter-repo command/tool detection, cleanup clone or rewrite validation flow in src.
Existing quick edits/rebase do not scrub arbitrary paths/replacements across history.

details.title: A graph that reads better (S).
details.source_text:
- [ ] **A graph that reads better (S).**
  - The Description column ends up about 120 px wide, while the Branch / Tag column takes about 260 px and is mostly empty. Give Description the flexible width, and let the ref column shrink when no pill is in view.
  - Summaries are cut hard with no ellipsis (`row.rs` uses a clip rect): "fix: CodeRabbit on f". Add an ellipsis and a tooltip with the whole message.
  - Lanes that have commits but no ref in view read as orphans. Give them a faint label, the ref's name or _detached_.
partial_coverage_notes: Dev already gives description residual width and ellipsizes body text. Remaining requested changes are adaptive ref width, summary ellipsis/full tooltip, lane labels.

Ellipsize overflowing summary and show full message tooltip; preserve body fading.
